name: Hemolytik2_search_peptides
description: Search Hemolytik 2.0 (Raghava lab, IIITD) for experimentally validated HEMOLYTIC / TOXIC peptide records. Filter by 'nature' (e.g. Antimicrobial, Anticancer, CPP), 'source' (source organism, e.g. Human), or 'seq' (sequence). Each record returns the peptide sequence, hemolytic activity (LC50/HC50 with units), source organism, origin, N/C-terminus and chemical (non-natural) modifications, linear/cyclic form, L/D chirality mix, length, nature, PubMed ID, and year. Use to assess peptide safety / hemolysis liability. Keyless public API.

dataType.description: Field to filter on. One of: 'nature' (peptide nature, e.g. Anticancer, Antimicrobial, CPP), 'source' (source organism, e.g. Human), or 'seq' (sequence). Default: 'nature'.

dataValue.description: Value to match for the chosen dataType. Examples: 'Anticancer' (with dataType=nature) -> ~166 records; 'Human' (with dataType=source) -> ~9255 records.

id.description: The database's own identifier for the peptide entry.

seq.description: The amino-acid sequence in one-letter code.

nter.description: N-terminal modification, e.g. acetylation. A free versus a blocked terminus changes stability and activity.

lyn_cyc.description: Whether the peptide is linear or cyclic.

nature.description: The peptide's class or origin as the database records it.

origin.description: Where the peptide came from -- the organism, or the design it was derived from.

source.description: The source the entry was taken from.

pmid.description: PubMed ID of the paper reporting it.

activity.description: The measured haemolytic activity -- what this database records.

non_hem.description: The non-haemolytic concentration, where reported. The gap between this and `activity` is the therapeutic window.

ldmix.description: Lipid or detergent mixture used in the assay. Haemolysis measured against different red-cell preparations is not comparable.

exp_str.description: The experimental conditions as free text.

oneOf.description: Matching hemolytic peptide records. Each has id, pmid, year, seq, name, cter, nter, lyn_cyc, ldmix, non_nat, length, nature, activity (e.g. 'LC50 =1.4 micromolar'), source, origin, exp_str, non_hem.
